To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we have developed SystemML which is a higher level language that enables users to express ML algorithms in a concise, declarative manner, 2) SystemML is a compilation system that compiles these ML algorithms to MapReduce jobs, and 3) we have developed several optimization strategies that enable efficient execution of these MapReduce jobs on a large cluster of machines.
SystemML can be used to efficiently execute ML algorithms on Mapreduce, and the performance is competitive with the performance of a specialized ML framework.
we present a system for declarative machine learning in MapReduce, and we evaluate its performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, implementation, and optimization of SystemML, a declarative ML language for large-scale data processing in MapReduce environments.
developing an efficient and scalable ML framework for MapReduce that is expressive enough to capture the broad range of ML algorithms.
making ML algorithms more accessible and scalable to run on large data and machine clusters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SystemML is the most efficient way of running ML algorithms on Mapreduce.
the performance is comparable to hand coded MapReduce jobs, but the ease with which ML algorithms can be expressed and executed in SystemML is much higher than hand coding MapReduce jobs.
SystemML is a promising approach to implement ML algorithms on Map Reduce clusters, and it can be very effective for some algorithms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SystemML provides a framework for declarative machine learning on large datasets and that it can provide significant speedups for several algorithms on large datasets.
SystemML can achieve up to 2x speedup over the state-of-the-art ML implementations on MapReduce.
SystemML enables a broad class of ML algorithms to be expressed and executed efficiently in MapReduce.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SystemML enables the rapid prototyping of ML algorithms in a MapReduce setting.

a higher level language that exposes linear algebra primitives and is compiled into a set of optimized MapReduce jobs can significantly simplify and improve the performance of a large class of supervised and un-supervised ML algorithms on Map Reduce.
a declarative ML language and compiler can be used to significantly reduce the development and execution costs of ML algorithms on a MapReduce cluster.
